data.solution_steps:
Part (a). The midline y=D is the average value of the oscillation. Here D=34, so the park averages \boxed{34\text{ thousand}} visitors per month.

Part (b). The amplitude is A=@A@, so the quantity rises @A@ above the average value and falls @A@ below it:

data.solution_steps:
Part (a). The midline y=D is the average value of the oscillation. Here D=45, so the park averages \boxed{45\text{ thousand}} visitors per month.

Part (b). The amplitude is A=@A@, so the quantity rises @A@ above the average value and falls @A@ below it:

\text{maximum}=45+18=63\text{ thousand}\qquad \text{minimum}=45-18=27\text{ thousand}

Part (c). Here B= rac{\pi}{6}, so the period is

data.solution_steps:
Part (a). The midline y=D is the average value of the oscillation. Here D=36, so the park averages \boxed{36\text{ thousand}} visitors per month.

data.solution_steps:
Part (a). The midline y=D is the average value of the oscillation. Here D=51, so the park averages \boxed{51\text{ thousand}} visitors per month.

Part (b). The amplitude is A=@A@, so the quantity rises @A@ above the average value and falls @A@ below it:

\text{maximum}=51+8=59\text{ thousand}\qquad \text{minimum}=51-8=43\text{ thousand}

the busiest month is May with 59\text{ thousand} visitors and the slowest is November with 43\text{ thousand}, so the range is \boxed{[43\text{ thousand},\ 59\text{ thousand}]}.

Part (c). Here B= rac{\pi}{6}, so the period is

\text{Period}=\frac{2\pi}{B}=\frac{2\pi}{\frac{\pi}{6}}=2\pi\cdot\frac{6}{\pi}=12

The period is \boxed{12} @index_unit@, and so visitation follows a yearly cycle and repeats every 12 months.

Part (d). The phase shift is the value of @var@ that makes the argument of the sine equal to zero:

\frac{\pi}{6}(x-2)=0 \implies x-2=0 \implies x=2

The phase shift is \boxed{2} months, and so the pattern is shifted 2 months to the right: attendance is at its average and climbing in February, peaks in May, and is lowest in November.

Part (e). Substitute x=4 (April):

V(4)=8\sin\left[\frac{\pi}{6}(4-2)\right]+51=8\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)+51=4 \, \sqrt{3} + 51 \approx 58\text{ thousand}

So the model predicts about \boxed{58\text{ thousand}} visitors in April.
